utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, there was another segment there that had a black screen and then what looked like a crate of ammunition. Can you tell us what -- what -- what's happening there?

Yes, this is another black segment, a public redacted part of the original raw material Petrovic. But we never received the footages from this redacted portion. And then we are coming to the recording of Mr. Petrovic, recording on the raw images. Just he -- he follows the two APCs on the road towards Pervani.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you -- if we could turn now to pages 34 and 35.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Blaszczyk on page 34 we have an image there with two different time stamps and some red dotted line there. Can you tell us what this image is?

Yes. We -- especially we -- we merged these two footage -- two stills from Petrovic video showing -- showing exactly the location when -- when the footage was recorded. And this is why we did it and this is why we have two different time stamps here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Ms. Stewart, if I could ask you to roll the Petrovic video once again from where we left off. If we could get the image on everyone's screens, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] You have two men from the other squad. "Who? "Lucic and the man with him."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We could stop right there. And that's at 00:12:45.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, can you tell us at this point is Mr. Borovcanin still with Mr. Petrovic?

Yes, correct. Mr. Borovcanin together with Mr. Petrovic. They are following these two APCs. And Mr. Petrovic is recording, yeah, the movement of these two APCs including -- we see also on this part of the footage Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we'll -- we'll play that on in just a moment, but can you tell us where along the road we are at this point? We've moved away from Sandici meadow?
Yeah. Yes. We moved away from Sandici meadow. We are towards Konjevic Polje road. We are located about 200 -- 2.800 metres from Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now we will continue playing the video and there will be another black screen. And that's, again, a deliberate black screen. And we'll just run it through. If Ms. Stewart can hit play on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart, if we could pause it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: A few things, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, we stopped it at 00:14:30.8.

I believe this is Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we heard some music. Where is that music coming from?
This music comes from the car belong to -- used by Mr. Borovcanin and Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we just back one screen shot. Back to the -- to the -- armoured vehicles, a little bit further. Okay. We can stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, again here we have a time stamp recorded. What can you tell us about the accuracy of that?
Yeah. Definitely this is 13 July 1995, and I believe based on the witness statements that it -- the time code is correct. This is 16:49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, can I ask the witness the following. Again and again we are talking about whether the time is accurate, yes or no. Because if you know the date, then, of course, it must be relatively easy to see, within certain limits, what the time is? I mean, shadows are the same every year on the 13th of July. The sun -- the position of the sun is the same, therefore the shadow should be the same as well. Have you ever -- because the question comes up again and again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is correct, Your Honour, we made some exercise but in relation to Kravica warehouse with shadow. But we didn't do that, I mean, just with the shadow, I mean just related to -- to Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, but the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the warehouse, you said, that's where you did it. Did it turn out to be accurate in -- or were you unable to establish it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not able to establish the exact time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- recorded but approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart, if we could now continue playing the video for a few more seconds, and this will take us to the next page in the road book.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We can pause it right there. And that's at 00:14:41.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, we saw a number of houses that appear to have been extracted by you here on page 36 in your road book, and tell us how you went about identifying the location of where Mr. Petrovic and Mr. Borovcanin were at this point in the video?

It is the position of these two APCs now and a little bit further down towards Konjevic Polje. We are in Pervani. It's about 300 metres further from the previous location. I was able to locate these four houses also depicted in Petrovic video. The houses were rebuilt, of course, in 2006, but if you look closely on the shape of the windows, roofs, and following the movement of the camera we see that we are referring to the same houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I am going to move on to another video segment and perhaps I have it correct now that it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now ten minutes past 1.00. We'll take a break after the witness has been escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.text: And we resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, before we continue, could you inform the Chamber where we are in terms of timing?

utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't anticipate I will finish today. utterances.text: And Ms. Stewart informed me that Mr. Blaszczyk is not scheduled to testify again until I believe it's the 14th of June, so that's when his examination will resume.

utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can --

utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that there is a rather rigid schedule for next week. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, if you could turn to and if we could all turn to page 38 and 39 in the stills book. I'm sorry, I misspoke again. It's not the stills book. It's the road book.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that's 65 ter 5759, pages 37 and 38 in the B/C/S in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We are going to see this footage of the houses that you've extracted. But looking at the photos you have taken on page 39, at least they appear to me to be a little bit different. In particular, if I can turn your attention to paragraph number 1. Could you please explain the difference here.

Your Honour, in 2006 I was able to -- to locate this, the place recorded by Mr. Petrovic in July of 1995. I was able to locate, in fact, one damaged house in -- in 2006. But to confirm the exact location, I talked to the owner of this house. In fact, the owner of the house next to this damaged house from 2006. I showed him the picture of the stills from Petrovic video and he was -- the owner of the house since the beginning, since before the war, even, he says that definitely this is his house, just that this picture depicted his houses. And we have one of these house on my picture from the page 39. This is on the picture 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So the other two houses in your photograph 1, just in front of the damaged house, those did not exist then at the time of the -- of the Petrovic video in July --
Yeah.

Yes, it is correct. These two houses were not existed at that time. In fact, one was built and the higher one was rebuilt after the war. And the -- let's say the smaller one was built after the war also.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you say "rebuilt," are you talking about the -- the unmarked house we see in images A and B on page 38?
Yes. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could continue watching the Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Yes, yes, but to avoid any surprises there won't be any --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we just pause it there momentarily, and that's 00:16:38.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, we now saw Mr. Borovcanin, Mr. Petrovic, we know were in Sandici meadow. They are moving along the road. You told us they were following the APCs. And now can you tell us where we've arrived? We've seen that the car started moving again. Where are they headed now?

These are the first footage we see the car moving towards Sandici and Kravica, from the direction of Pervani and Konjevic Polje. It is the first footage recorded by Mr. Petrovic, Pirocanac, during his movement on the road Konjevic Polje-Sandici-Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Are you saying that they have turned around at this point?

Yes. In fact, not exactly on this point because as we see I located this -- this -- this location. This is -- I spotted this location. This is about 2.000 metres from Sandici meadow itself, but the previous picture we saw these two APC. It was recorded about 3.000 metres from Sandici meadow. It means further down towards Konjevic Polje. But Mr. Pirocanac, Petrovic, started to record his video again while being in this location, this particular location. This is about 2.000 metres from Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, at some time which you haven't been able to determine with precision, the car is moving towards Konjevic Polje, turns around, and is now moving back to Sandici where they were?

Yes, this is correct. I can say only -- yeah, we can see here that the last footage recorded by Mr. Petrovic on the way toward Konjevic Polje was done in Pervani. We see these two APCs on the road. This is the last footage under -- on his movement towards Konjevic Polje. The first movement towards -- the first recorded movement towards Sandici meadow returning way -- this spot, 2.000 metres from Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I could start Ms. Stewart if we could start replaying this again about 10 seconds before this point. A little bit -- that's fine, thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Yes, yes, but to avoid any surprises. "There won't be any. "Take this tanker to the building and leave it there. I need it there. "Your tanker is waiting here. "Officer Bor. "I'm listening. "Stop the traffic behind you. "Kovac said he would do it. "I know."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we just pause it right there, please. This is 00:17:00.1. And the transcript reference for the conversation there is on page 10 in the English and page 11 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, there is a couple of things I want to ask you about that conversation we've just heard. First there was a reference to a column moving. Throughout the course of your investigation, are you able to tell us what that is a reference to?

Yes, during the course of our investigation we are able to establish that they are referring to the column of the prisoners of the Muslim men captured in -- near Sandici meadow and taken from Sandici meadow to Kravica warehouse. And this is conversation about -- most probably about this column and it has been confirmed by various witnesses, even by the witness who was a member was Sekovici detachment who itself stopped the traffic, you know, just on -- in -- in the place of Kravica, in the centre of Kravica village. His name is Milenko Pepic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And how is it possible that we're actually hearing this conversation?

As -- as we notice before, the radio was installed in Mr. Borovcanin car. We saw the aerial of the radio on his car in -- near Sandici meadow. He use his -- his car radio. And they have for their disposal also the handsets.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now it may be easy just to see this. If we could pull up the transcript, in fact, because this is a rolling transcript. If we could display page 10 in English, 11 in the B/C/S. And this is attached to 65 ter 22422. So it's an attachment to the video, the Petrovic video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now as that comes up, Mr. Blaszczyk, we see the acronym "LJB" on the transcript and the transcript itself tells us it's Ljubisa Borovcanin. Can you confirm that he is engaged in that conversation?
Yes, I can confirm this is Ljubisa Borovcanin words. Even I recognise his voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We still don't have that on the screen, but we have Mr. Borovcanin saying, "Oficir Bor." Can you tell us what "oficir" is a reference to?

Oficir, this is a nickname of Rade Cuturic, who was a commander of the Sekovici detachment, the police Sekovici detachment. And Bor it was code-name or name used by his subordinates of Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you could just clarify for us how it is that you know that, that, in fact, these are their -- these are these individuals?

As I said, during the course of our investigation we talked to many people, many members of Sekovici detachment and the police. And also if Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin himself, he confirmed that this is a Bor is referring to him and oficir is the nickname of Rade Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now we have just after that NMG. This is recorded as unidentified male voice on Motorola 1 saying -- Motorola 2 - I'm sorry - saying: "I'm listening." And Mr. Borovcanin saying: "Stop the traffic behind on you." Can you tell us do you know who the male voice is? Have you determined that through the course of your investigation, and explaining to us what is meant here by "stop the traffic behind you"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm confused. If it's identified as unidentified, I don't know -- I guess they are asking for specification unless we have some -- some foundation for this. I'm really having a hard time figuring out how to approach this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness is invited to tell us whether he knows who the male voice is and how he knows it. That -- so we'll listen to the answer. And, of course, he's not invited to speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I said, I know quite well the voice of Mr. Borovcanin. And I believe this is the voice of Mr. Borovcanin, "Stop the traffic behind you." And the other unidentified man on the Motorola, I believe this is Cuturic. But I based my observation on the later conversation that somebody -- somebody from the car, you know, saying I think -- I don't remember now, but somebody saying that that oficir is speaking. Oficir, this is the nickname of Cuturic. And in regards to -- to stopping the traffic, you know, just, I believe -- and Borovcanin I believe also confirm it in his statement that he's referring to the traffic need to be stopped in Kravica village.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you know where Mr. Cuturic is at this point in time?
Yes. Mr. Cuturic is in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you -- now, he's instructed to stop the traffic by Mr. Borovcanin. Can you tell us in terms of your investigation what traffic are we talking about?

Yeah. We established that a few witnesses, they are talking about, including Milenko Pepic who stopped the traffic, in fact. He said that it was related to the movement of -- of the buses and trucks with population from Potocari. They were transported along this road towards Tisca.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just for clarification, when you say the movement of the population from Potocari, you are referring to which population exactly?
I am referring to Muslim population, to women and children and old men who were separated from men in Potocari and they were put in the buss and trucks and then transported to Tisca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of this location we are transported to because we have now two different recordings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I am referring to Tisca. This is the place located near Kladanj. Tisca, T-i-s-c-a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now the traffic is being stopped around Kravica. Can you tell us what's happening at Kravica?

Yes. As we know -- as we established, in Kravica warehouse there were -- the Muslim who were kept in Kravica warehouse, they were killed over there inside the warehouse. And also we see it on edited version of Petrovic video, we see that -- we see that the bodies in front of the Kravica warehouse. People were killed we established by the members of the Sekovici detachment and the police and probably at least one member of the army took the part in killings.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you say that the population, the men that were in the Kravica warehouse were killed, are you able to tell us whether this, in fact, was happening around the time this conversation takes place about stopping the traffic after -- or what do you know about the timing of that?

In fact, I am not sure. We are not sure whether the killings happened at -- in -- actually in this time when they -- there was conversation about stopping the traffic. But definitely it -- it happened shortly after that. If we follow the recordings of Mr. Petrovic, we can count minutes and seconds, you know, just, and then we can follow the Petrovic raw footage. We see that there is the blank portion of -- of -- of his footage or overrecorded portion of his footage where we are supposed to have this Kravica incident. But later on if we play the Petrovic video on -- in Sandici, when he recorded events in Sandici before going towards Kravica, we hear some shooting from machine-guns. And also if we have good quality of the video we can also hear two explosions, at least two explosion of hand grenades. I believe that they are hand grenades. I believe at that time execution occurred in Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. So we are going -- Mr. Borovcanin and Petrovic are going to -- Mr. Petrovic are going to be moving down the road towards Sandici where we will watch what you've just described for us. In between that, though, we see some images from their journey along that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if we could turn now to the road book at page 40 and 41. And this is 65 ter 5759. It's pages 39 and 40 in the B/C/S version. That's for e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blaszczyk, we see here that you've captured some images from the video showing some armed uniformed soldiers. Have -- do you know what units they belong to?
Yes. These soldiers, according to the statement of the witnesses, they were the part of -- of MUP forces. Most likely the members of Jahorina, Jahorina unit, from training centre in Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And tell us where -- where we find ourselves now and how you were able to identify where these men are standing on the road?

We are in the village of Lolici, this is the village located from Sandici meadow, about 1.900 metres. And we see the wall, the retaining wall. The wall still exist in the same shape and the same location. If we compare the shape of the wall this is the same location, and following of course the movement of the camera.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's turn the page. So we're on 42 and 43 in the hard copy, 41 and 42 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, can you also explain here. We see some quite -- I mean, some of these images are quite blurred. Can you tell us how come that is and how you were, despite that, able to identify where these men are standing or located?

Mr. Borovcanin and Petrovic, of course, they are driving in their car towards Sandici now. And because of the movement of the car and because of due to his equipment he had, for the recordings, he was not able to have very clear picture of the people standing along the road. But talking to the members of Jahorina unit, talking to the members of other MUP units which were placed in this location, we are sure -- we know that this -- these people belonged to Jahorina unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And --

Without knowing their name, of course, but because Jahorina unit, it was the unit containing - how to say? - deserters from Bosnia who were later on captured on the territory of the Serbia and forced -- by force taken to Bosnia again and put in the unit, MUP unit training centre in Jahorina. Later on, this unit was deployed on the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now is the retaining wall that we see on page 43, is that the same retaining wall that we saw on the previous page?
No, it's not the same wall because if we drive through this area we see -- we see -- we see quite many of these kind of the walls but not the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And so I take it, then, that this is a retaining wall that's a little bit further along from the previous one; is that correct?
Yes, this is correct. It's closer to Sandici meadow than the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now on page 43 we see here what you've marked as X, a white X, and you've got a description on the bottom there that it relates to an exhumation. Can you tell us a little bit about that and your marking?

Yes. We know that in this -- this place, which were marked by X and in white colour, exhumation was conducted in June 2004 by Bosnia federal commission for missing persons. And during this exhumation I believe, as I could remember, about 17 -- 17 bodies were exhumed. And, Your Honour, we know it also from the witnesses that some execution took place in Sandici meadow itself. Whether the people were killed in Sandici meadow or near Sandici meadow, we were not able to establish it for 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Moving on to page 44 in the hard copy and page 45.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's 43 and 44 on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Again we see another image here of a soldier and it's pretty clear that you've marked that on -- on the road. And just remind us now how far we've travelled and how close we are to Sandici.
In this picture we are coming closer to Sandici meadow. We are about 250 metres from Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Turning the page again to page 46 and page 47, we see -- we see more soldiers and, again, you've -- you've marked here that they are about 200 metres from Sandici meadow. And I'd like to ask you about the photograph on page 47 marked number 2. It's a -- we see the whole road in photograph number 1, the winding road, we see you've marked Sandici meadow in this destroyed white house. Now, the photograph 2 looks like it's going in a circle. Can -- is that the case or what's happening there?

Yes, you -- Your Honour, I would like to clarify. It looks like a cycle but in reality it looking a little bit different. This is a bending road but because we merged two photos, we did, in fact, panorama photos of this particular segment of the road, and this looks a little bit like a cycle but in reality it is a rather straight one having, of course, the curve later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. Let's then turn the page to pages 48 and 49 in the hard copy, 47 and 48 on e-court for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now here we see that - and we'll watch this clip in a moment - but we see that in image B Mr. Borovcanin has stepped out of the car. Tell us what's happened now in terms of Mr. Petrovic and Borovcanin's travel?

Mr. Borovcanin left the car -- they stopped the car, in fact, near Sandici meadow. Mr. Borovcanin walked towards Sandici meadow. He talked to his soldiers on the spot. And Mr. Petrovic, Pirocanac, is recording the events around -- around this place.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And --
We are very near Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we can see that on page 49 you've indicated there position vis-a-vis Sandici meadow and the Kravica warehouse as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could start playing the Petrovic video. If we could start at 17 -- 17 minutes and 30. Yeah, if we could start rolling that video from here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Come over here there is something. "There is more up there. "Come on, fellows. Come out. Come on, fellows. Come out. Just put your hands in the air. Come on. "Hurry up. "About 50 will. About 50 from this slope for sure. "Ha? "From that slope about 50 of them should come down. "Behind that slope. "Yes. "Come on, fellows. Come out. Mother fuckers. "How many have already come out so far? "Well, about, 3- to 4.000, surely. "They all surrender to you here? "Yes. "When I say this in Belgrade, they usually say an exaggerated number. "Well, it is exaggerated. Of course it is. "But how many of them are there? "Yes. That many, that many."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we just pause it here for a minute. This is at 00:19:09.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blaszczyk, during the course of the investigation, have you been able to identify this individual?
Yes, this is member of Jahorina unit. I do not recall his name now. But definitely he is member of Jahorina unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now he -- he makes a reference to them having 3.000 -- that 3.000 to 4.000 have surrendered. In terms of that figure and your investigation, does that figure sound about right?

Yes. During your investigation, reviewing the statements of the witnesses and -- yeah, I believe that the figure is quite right. At this time of day, 13th of July, afternoon, that they may have about few thousand of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can continue with the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, I need seven minutes, approximately, to deliver a decision. So before we enter a new area, perhaps. You were about to do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. We can stop right here. I'll just make a note of the time. We're at 00:19:10.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Blaszczyk, we'll not be able to conclude your examination-in-chief today. I do understand that you're scheduled to come back on the 14th, you said -- 14th of June because we have a rather strict schedule for next week. Meanwhile, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given already or whether that's testimony still to be given upon your return. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, as was the case with Ms. Gallagher when she testified, Mr. Blaszczyk is an investigator within the OTP and to some extent -- in the same extent as Ms. Gallagher, there may be some normal communication but not relating to his testimony and we'd just ask for the same -- the same instructions that applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the Defence did not -- not to speak about the testimony, not to speak about the subject matter of the testimony, and not a strict prohibition to exchange a word with -- with others. But you should take it very strict, Mr. Blaszczyk, so not to communicate in any way about matters on which you are testifying here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then having given you these instructions, you can follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back. It will be communicated to you exactly when, but I do understand the 14th of June. But we could immediately start with your testimony, we'll see at that date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, I will deliver a decision on behalf of this Chamber. The Chamber delivers its decision on the Prosecution's notice of disclosure of expert report of six forensic expert witnesses pursuant to Rule 94 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, filed on the 7th of November, 2012, concerning witnesses Jose Pablo Baraybar, John Clark, William Haglund, Chris Lawrence, Fredy Peccerelli, and Richard Wright. On the 10th of December, 2012, the Chamber granted the Defence request of 30 November, 2012, for an extension of time to file its Rule 94 bis(B) notice until the 21st of January, 2013. After an informal communication by the Chamber requesting the Prosecution's submission on how it I intended to tender these witnesses' evidence in light of the absence of a Defence notice, on the 29th of January, 2013, the Defence made submissions in court to the effect that it required more time to file its notice. The Chamber directed the parties to discuss scheduling matters of these witnesses and to inform the Chamber of the outcome of such discussions, accordingly. This can be found at transcript pages 7650 to 7651. Further communications between the parties and the Chamber followed in court on the 18th of February, informally on the 22nd and the 28th of February, and by means of a reminder to the parties in court on the 1st of March, 2013, for an update. Not having received any further submissions from the parties on the matter, the Chamber, per informal communication on the 28th of March, 2013 - put on the record on the 8th of April of 2013 at transcript page 9521 - informed the Defence that it was expected to file its Rule 94 bis(B) notice by the 22nd of April, 2013, which the Defence did. In its notice, the Defence challenges the methodology and reliability of all of the proffered reports, submitting moreover that some of the conclusions reached therein lack crucial information required by the Defence to properly challenge the reports. The Defence requests that the Prosecution either be ordered to supplement its submissions in this regard, reserving the right to fully challenge the reports once a proper application has been submitted. Alternatively, the Defence opposes admission into evidence of the said reports, and requests the opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses. The Defence does not challenge the expertise of the six witnesses. Upon review of their CVs, the Chamber is satisfied that they have specialised knowledge. Such knowledge may be of assistance to the Chamber in assessing the evidence to be presented by the Prosecution on the exhumation of grave-sites related to the alleged killings of Bosnian Muslims following the fall of Srebrenica. It therefore considers Witnesses Baraybar, Haglund, Peccerelli, as experts in the field of forensic anthropology; Witnesses Clark and Lawrence as experts in the field of forensic pathology; and Witness Wright as an expert in the field of forensic archeology, for the purpose of their anticipated evidence before the Chamber. The Chamber notes that the Defence has not provided any specification as to the additional information it would require to properly challenge the proffered reports of these witnesses, as submitted. In its latest witness schedule, the Prosecution has planned for the potential testimony of these witnesses to start in the second week of July 2013. The Defence will have the full opportunity to further explore the alleged flaws in methodology and reliability of the respective reports at that stage. The Chamber hereby decides, pursuant to Rule 94 bis of the Rules, that Jose Pablo Baraybar, John Clark, William Haglund, Christopher Lawrence, Fredy Peccerelli, and Richard Wright may be called to testify as expert witnesses, and shall be made available for cross-examination by the Defence. The Chamber defers its decision on admission into evidence of the tendered reports for these witnesses until the time of their respective testimonies. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. We adjourn for the day and we will resume Tuesday, the 28th of May, at 9.30 in the morning, if I'm not mistaken, in this same courtroom III. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
